clue.text: It involves quickly lapping baby milk before lunchtime

parts.note: formula is powdered or ready-made milk for infants
one o'clock is a typical time for lunch

explanation.surface: A baby greedily laps up its bottle of milk just before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lapping' suggests a drinking infant, but it means going round a racing circuit; lunchtime is one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Formula One motor racing is a sport whose cars complete fast circuits of a track, so speedy laps are central to it.

clue.text: Duke in good health embracing son

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: fit means healthy
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An aristocrat in fine fettle hugs his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman, but 'put up your dukes' uses it as slang for a hand clenched to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes is slang for fists, from rhyming slang Duke of Yorks for forks, meaning hands.

clue.text: Substitute Salah on hour completely upset shape

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, and completely applies it to everything before

parts.note: a sub is a substitute player
Mo Salah is the Egyptian Liverpool footballer
hr is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A footballer comes on as a substitute after an hour, and the whole team is thrown into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts MO above HR; the whole string SUBMOHR is then turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure, a parallelogram whose four sides are equal in length.

clue.text: Upper-class wrinkled mod lazily covering old Dylan classic

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the jumbled letters enclose another
lazily suggests a sloppy, careless arrangement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A posh, crumpled mod idles over an old Bob Dylan record.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan suggests Bob, but this is the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Milk Wood is the celebrated radio play for voices by Welsh poet Dylan Thomas, a recognised literary masterpiece.

clue.text: Gloop one famously served in Rome?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the greedy boy in Roald Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
second meaning: the first Roman emperor, whom the empire served

explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' hints at food for the gluttonous Gloop, but the emperor was the one being served.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus Gloop is Dahl's greedy chocolate-eating child, and Augustus was the first emperor of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Tender dogfish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look after someone sick
second meaning: a kind of shark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an adjective describing the fish, but it is a verb meaning to care for.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to care for a patient, and the nurse hound or nurse shark is a small shark called a dogfish.

clue.text: Possesses hard drug

parts.note: possesses means has
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone is caught in possession of a hard drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a short informal name for hashish, the cannabis resin smoked as a narcotic.

clue.text: Tombstone found in this state?

parts.note: surface reading: a grave marker turns up somewhere
setter's reading: the Wild West town of the OK Corral, which lies in a southwestern US state

explanation.definitionFit: Tombstone, scene of the gunfight at the OK Corral, is a town in this southwestern American state bordering Mexico.

clue.text: Churchman who's had too much communion wine?

definitions.text: Churchman who's had too much communion wine?

parts.words: Churchman who's had too much communion wine?
parts.note: surface reading: a cleric who is drunk on sacramental wine
setter's reading: a senior religious leader, punningly intoxicated

explanation.definitionFit: A high priest is a chief religious official, and high is slang for intoxicated, so a tipsy cleric fits both senses.

clue.text: Tired, retreating Yankee leaves D-Day beach

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read from its end
when something leaves it departs, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: tired and sleepy
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A weary American soldier pulls back from a Normandy landing beach.
explanation.walkthrough: DROWSY loses its Y to leave DROWS, which is then read backwards to give SWORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sword was the codename of the easternmost of the Normandy landing beaches assaulted by British troops in June 1944.

clue.text: Activity yielding ginger and nuts?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the preceding words are scrambled wildly

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pastime that produces a crop of ginger root and nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like part of the harvest alongside ginger, but it is the signal to rearrange 'ginger and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardening is a hobby or pastime, and one that can indeed produce ginger and nuts, giving the clue an all-in-one flavour.

clue.text: Broadcast on air X-rated track, remarkable

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: An adult-rated song played on the radio causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'on air' both sound like radio talk; only 'Broadcast' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary means very unusual or exceptional, so worthy of note.

clue.text: Starter home built for flighty character, very excited

parts.note: a creature that flies builds a nest as its home
very means so, as in 'so happy'
up means excited or keyed-up

explanation.surface: A starter home is built for a giddy, flighty person who is thrilled about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter home' reads as a first house, but 'Starter' alone is the definition, a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird's-nest soup, a Chinese delicacy made from swiftlet nests, is served as a first course of a meal.

clue.text: Fresh hake wrapped in shirt? That's novel!

indicators.note: wrapped in means placed inside something

parts.note: a blouse is a shirt

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the fish's letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh fish wrapped in a shirt: what an unusual idea!
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's novel!' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but 'novel' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a famous book by Charles Dickens, a work of long fiction.

clue.text: Sweet soul music played with Mike unplugged

indicators.note: played suggests music performed freely, so the letters are rearranged
unplugged means disconnected, so that letter is removed from the music

parts.note: taken as written
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Smooth soul is performed acoustically, with the microphone unplugged.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing M from SOUL MUSIC leaves eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Luscious describes something richly sweet and delicious in taste, like ripe fruit.

clue.text: South American returning service — I watch big game here

parts.note: SA is an abbreviation for South America or South American

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for service is read backwards

parts.note: the Royal Air Force is one of the armed services
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South American back from military service says he goes to view big game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker's pronoun but is simply a letter; the RAF is Britain's air force.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, typically in Africa, to observe or hunt large wild animals.

clue.text: Forceful English parliamentarian in charge introducing cap?

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the cap goes inside

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a Member of Parliament
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: An English politician in charge is bringing in a cap on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' suggests a limit an MP might impose, but it is headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means expressed with force and clarity, so vigorous and insistent.

clue.text: Unfortunately kinda empty region

parts.note: alas expresses regret, much like unfortunately

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: only the first and last letters of kinda are kept

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a place is sort of deserted, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is a US state, a large area of territory, which the clue loosely calls a region.

clue.text: Ref somewhat irregular, bit erratic

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of, so the answer is a portion of the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of irregular, all of bit and the start of erratic

explanation.surface: A football fan complains the referee has been inconsistent and a little unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is an official judge who settles disputes, which is exactly what an arbiter is.

clue.text: This compiler, flipping angry, first to sue airline

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the compiler's word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
irate means angry

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of sue

explanation.surface: The setter, furious, is the first to take legal action against a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive before 'angry', but it turns ME around.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirates is the Dubai-based international carrier, one of the world's largest flying companies.

clue.text: Quiver male soprano carries

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the singer contains the other letter

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A boy singer's voice wavers as he carries the high notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver is to shake slightly, which is what trembling means.

clue.text: Boy's plum put on cooker? Take it or leave it

parts.note: a hob is the cooking surface on top of a stove
a boy is a son
a plum job is a choice one, the best

explanation.surface: A boy's plum is set on the stove to cook, with a shrug about whether you want it.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'put on' places the boy's plum after HOB, the British word for a stovetop.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobson's choice is an idiom for a free choice that is no real choice at all: accept the offer or get nothing.

clue.text: Prosecuted electronic Britpop band

parts.note: to be sued is to face legal action
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A music group playing electronic Britpop faces a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Britpop was the 1990s British guitar-pop scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede were a leading 1990s British indie rock group fronted by Brett Anderson.

clue.text: Force Germany to engage European Union in bitter battle

indicators.note: to engage here means to take hold of, so the letters grip the union between them

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
EU is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Germany is compelled to take on the European Union in a fierce conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a prolonged and bitter quarrel or hostility between parties.

clue.text: Least well organised? It's United, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football fan laments that United are the most shambolic team.
explanation.walkthrough: United is a common short name for clubs such as Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidiest is the superlative of untidy, meaning most messy and disordered, so least neatly arranged.

clue.text: Stroll bet loses grand

indicators.note: loses means drops, so a letter is removed from the bet

parts.note: to bet is to gamble
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A walk to the bookies ends with a wager losing a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, a leisurely walk.

clue.text: Noble, tragic King left at the back

indicators.note: left is the letter L, and at the back says that letter moves from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A tragic monarch abandoned in the rear: a scene from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The L that starts LEAR moves to the end, giving EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British aristocrat ranking above a viscount, so a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Very white, Cliff has pain in the noggin after draining bottle

indicators.note: draining empties the inside, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of bottle
having pain is being achy
noggin is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Cliff wakes with a hangover after emptying a bottle, looking pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff looks like a man's name, but it is the landform; read 'be achy head' after the drained bottle. Beachy Head is a chalk headland on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Beachy Head in Sussex is a famous sheer chalk headland, so a gleaming white seaside precipice.
